title: Caligula
objective: After this level you can separate what is known about Caligula from later rumor.
summary: Caligula, “little boot,” began popular in 37 CE and became autocratic. His own guard killed him in 41 CE. Many tales about him are hostile rumor.

cards.headline: Most of what you’ve heard about Caligula was written by people who hated him.
cards.body: So what can we actually trust? Start with a nickname, end with a murder, and read the gossip in between with care.

cards.headline: Little Boot
cards.body: Gaius became emperor in 37 CE, but everyone knows him by a nickname. As a child he lived in his father’s army camp, wearing a small soldier’s uniform, and the soldiers called him Caligula, “little boot.” Imagine ruling an empire under your childhood nickname. He was popular at first. Then his rule turned autocratic and extravagant.

cards.headline: Consider the source
cards.body: Here’s the trouble with Caligula’s legend: most accounts of him come from later writers who were hostile to him. So historians treat the wildest stories with caution. Take the famous one about his plan to make his horse a consul. It may be a joke, or an exaggeration. Before you ask whether a story is true, ask who wrote it.
cards.callout: Ask who wrote a story, and why

mascot.line: Ask who wrote it before you ask if it’s true. You’ll use this again in Level 98.

cards.fact: Caligula was murdered by officers of his own guard in 41 CE.
cards.context: Remember the Praetorian Guard from Level 51, the bodyguard stationed in Rome? The men meant to protect the emperor ended his reign after just four years. This part of the story isn’t gossip.

options.label: little soldier
options.rationale: Close, but it was about his footwear.

questions.explanation: Soldiers called the child Gaius “little boot” because of his small uniform.

questions.prompt: Why do historians doubt many stories about Caligula?

options.label: He banned all history writing during his reign
The stories were all written in Greek
His coins show he was a gentle ruler
They come from later writers who hated him

questions.explanation: Hostile later writers had reasons to exaggerate, so their wildest claims need caution.

questions.prompt: Put Caligula’s life in order, from first to last.
items: Lived in his father’s army camp
Murdered by officers of his own guard
questions.explanation: As a child Caligula lived in his father’s army camp. He became emperor in 37 CE and was murdered by officers of his own guard in 41 CE.
